summary: Glacier NP lookout on Reynolds Ridge: built 1931, staffed 1951, abandoned 1953, burned by park rangers in 1962 or destroyed in 1963 (sources differ).

facts.design: Two-story National Park Service cab, a ready-cut house from Superior Buildings Company of Kalispell, with an Osborne fire finder
facts.status_note: Burned by park rangers in 1962 per Missoulian and Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com, SummitPost and the Huckleberry Hiker blog give 1963.

events.note: Erected June 1931 by the National Park Service; firelookout.com records a two-story cab.
Missoulian says the lookout opened in 1932, a year after the 1931 construction date in the other sources.
Mrs. Robert Bloedel and her husband, an Idaho State college student, were the lookouts on Mount Reynolds (Hungry Horse News item, quoted by Forest Lookouts).
Abandoned when the National Park Service switched to aerial fire monitoring.
Forest Lookouts gives 28 November 1962 for the burning, no longer needed. The Missoulian also says park rangers burned it in 1962.
Firelookout.com, SummitPost and the Huckleberry Hiker blog list it as destroyed in 1963.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Most sources date construction to 1931, and the Forest Lookouts page quotes a June 1931 erection. The Missoulian says the lookout opened in 1932. No source explains the gap, so the story gives both.
Forest Lookouts (28 November 1962) and the Missoulian give 1962. Firelookout.com, SummitPost and the Huckleberry Hiker blog give 1963. The story reports both and does not pick one.
Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives 48.66781, -113.66952, which matches the record. SummitPost GPS is 48.66791, -113.66782, about 125 m east. Record kept as is.

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict (1931 build vs 1932 opening; 1962 burning vs 1963 destruction) and both are reported. The 1931 erection is quoted secondhand through Forest Lookouts from an annual forestry report. SummitPost coordinates differ from the list by about 125 m; the record is kept. The Missoulian caption also describes a construction-crew photo, but no image URL was reachable, so no photos entry. Access left unknown; no source describes the site today.
